executive_summary: This packet closes the run at the workflow level: judge and pathway closure are closed, no workflow-owned blockers or deferrals remain, every fatal-severity row is fixed or superseded by a fixed row, and no repair recurred after its fix. The verdict is publishable-pending-owner-approval; the remaining actions are the owner's personal mathematical audit, the deliberate status:published changes, and push/deployment. Interpretively, the repair history splits between contract/metadata synchronization and genuine mathematical corrections — refined hypotheses, tightened citations, and several rewritten inferences — concentrated in the instrumental-variables/LATE chain, the Gaussian-regression and design-matrix dimension arguments, and executable-check contracts. The mathematics is as strong as the workflow can make it, but two things temper sign-off: the configured judge set's exact evidence covers the refreshed versions (all keeps) while the rest of the corpus rests on retained verdicts from an earlier epoch, and the runtime-class fixes were made at the tool layer, so the owner should re-run the smoke checks once. With no deferrals, no pathway obligations, and no repeated repairs, no further engine work is implied — only the owner gate.
caveats: Current-lineup judge evidence is exact only for the refreshed versions, where every verdict is a keep; the rest of the scope is supported by retained verdicts from an earlier review epoch, which are evidence rather than current coverage. The owner's personal audit remains the compensating check.

The adjudication stream contained false positives and confirmed nonfatal findings alongside fatal ones, so raw judge rejections overstate the defect picture; trust the adjudicated dispositions, not rejection totals.

A superseded historical row still reads as open — a published-audit note states the finding 'remains unresolved and deferred to owner' although a later row records it fixed — so read superseding dispositions and current frontmatter rather than historical notes.

Runtime-class findings (wrong gate signatures, unregistered computation names, ignored nested inputs) were repaired at the tool/contract layer; the packet records repaired contracts, not an owner-side re-run, so re-execute the smoke checks before publishing.

Closure is a workflow property, not mathematical truth: it means every routed defect is fixed or superseded, judge pairs are complete, and the defect history is cumulative across the whole run, so a row's presence does not imply the defect survived to current content.

Two silent-runtime findings concerned intermediate run reports rather than content (a wrong inventory ID and omitted consumer dispositions, both fixed); prefer the engine-rendered packet and on-disk ledgers over narrative reports when auditing.
